song.title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-flat minor, Op. 23 — I. Introduction (opening)

printedReferences: Jurgenson, sixth author revision, private full-score pp2–17
Eulenburg No.709 / E.E.3809, private full-score pp1–19
source.review: Legacy print-review.json retains 1836 rows with eight group-level note strings; these are not individual observations. Review3 is dynamics-only, with individual marks in private dynamics-review.json; prior pitch corrections retained without a new pitch proof.

notes: Boundary: Introduction only: source records 1–109, printed bars 1–108 plus unnumbered X1 inside the bar-48 cadenza. Allegro con spirito begins source record 110 / printed 109 and is excluded. Verified at Eulenburg p19–20 (e-021/022), Jurgenson p17 (j-018). Eulenburg counts the free cadenza continuation as an extra bar: file49 is Eulenburg50, and file109 is Eulenburg110. This numbering difference adds no music.

Transposition: clarinets -2, horns -7, F trumpets +5, double bass -12. Printed F trumpet opening in treble clef is the high-F instrument (+5); simultaneous brass voicing and register are audited separately from pitch classes.

Shared wind staves: simultaneous distinct voices split by voice; same-voice chords high/low even inside a polyphonic bar (e.g. horns4); single notes in an explicitly polyphonic bar retain their voice; whole-bar other-voice rests cover every later attack. All 39 original a2 candidates were compared with the print: 38 spurious duplications removed, bassoon unison at76 retained.
Piano: printed dynamics use the common marking for both hands. Velocity map pp39/p51/mp64/mf80/f99/ff115/fff126; no blanket maximum-velocity opening override.

Dynamics review3: every part has a continuous level curve. A ramp starts from the currently reached level and holds its endpoint; compatible printed target within3 quarters is approached. Without a target, a wedge changes22 velocity units (limited25..126). Same-direction overlapping word/wedge continuations merge. Piano marks between staves govern both hands; no independently engraved staff dynamics were identified in this opening. Piano98-100 diminuendo is one descent to the final sounding pp101. Explicit sustained-note points prevent a long tie from beginning its crescendo before the printed mark.

Hidden layers are evidence, not noise: the print decides when layers disagree. At48 the three hidden voice-3 eight-note chords replace the incorrect visible realization, as verified by the lead against Jurgenson p7. All pitch changes are in corrections.json; arpeggio rolls and real hand repartition are retained. All remaining hidden/visible differences in this opening were compared against the print; redundant hidden realizations are excluded only after that comparison.

Piano hand starts from voice 1–4 right / 5–8 left. When that split exceeds five fingers or a major tenth, repartition simultaneous pitches between hands without changing pitch/onset; before/after is in corrections.json. Cross-staff lower voice at63–71/77 therefore moves to the left where needed. Simultaneous identical keys merge, preserving sourceVoices. No sounding note may be discarded by the motion planner.

Tuplets use written type/dots × normal/actual exactly once, correcting the source integer-division rounding and its within-voice drift; every changed value is recorded in corrections.json. Grace groups precede the principal by at most .24 quarter; arpeggios use .32 quarter. Opening tuplet/grace/arpeggio passages were compared with both printed witnesses; the numerical roll/grace offsets are performance choices, with every piano attack verified in real geometry.
Pedal: 180 source marks -> 80 intervals in the opening; no derived intervals. start/resume down, stop/discontinue up, change releases then re-pedals after .035 quarter.

Tempo: retain the existing chosen opening base quarter=88, not the old full-movement +8% adjustment. Source playback 70 is not a printed metronome indication. Accelerando32–37:88→104; ritenuto37–39:104→88; a tempo40 beat2.5=104. Solo ornamental half-beat ascents41/42/44/45/46 use42 (42:34; 44:40) only over the run, then104. Cadenza48=74, X1=90, 49 upper run48 then90. Tempo I50=88; poco ritenuto59 beat2.5=80, a tempo61 beat2.5=88, rallent101→102:88→68, morendo106=64, final108=60. No duration-target stretching.

Fermatas use encoded ranges except the final collective rest: hold last quarter of108 for1.7s, keep hornIV through its full dotted half, then conductor cutoff and 4.1s hall/release tail. No109 attack.

String chord tones retained in sound; up to four separate motion voices are distributed over the existing 34 string seats, including every middle note. This is an explicit separate-seat performance choice for engraved chords without divisi labels; every note remains assigned. Full opening bow/finger geometry is checked separately, without changing printed notation. Full-movement development/reprise/cadenza interpretation is removed.

Keep accepted theme/tutti buses and master headroom. Extend piano lead+3dB through61, ending before62. Plan79-86 piano P90 at strings-2dB using the accepted meter and measured source voicing change. Apply quiet exposure+4dB to all87-108, including solo95-101; sparse102 gets a further2dB exposure before103. Brass morendo106-end is continuous0 to-14dB, independent of printed pp.

New audio has not been rendered here: target every87-108 mixP90 within30dB of loudest barP90;79-86 soloP90 within4dB below strings;108 P90>=8dB below105 and monotonic106-108; retain accepted median theme/tutti limits and raw ceiling.

Retain accepted32000Hz piano decoding and used-region prefix cuts; original files/layers intact. Lead measured468.055MB, cut/uncut0.03dB and >16kHz energy55dB below mix before this dynamics/performance revision. New selected files, memory and levels require new control/cut renders.

Solo performance is separate pv/pianoDb, leaving corrected printed v and every pitch/onset/duration/hand unchanged. Melody+0.65, bass-1.25, inner-3.2pv; first bass62-77+0.45, phrase-0.8..+0.65, ascending tuplets-1.1..+1.1, fixed seed+/-0.18. Printed phrase/response windows use their first actual upper-line pitch maximum as apex. Source-calibrated gain adds0.75dB per pv unit; inner/bass attenuation keeps them at least2.5/1dB under the chord melody, accented chords+1.2dB. No additional audio voices. Exact windows/contributions are in solo.performance and each piano note.
